summary: Canada admits visa-exempt nationals arriving by air with an eTA (CAD 7, valid up to 5 years), lets US citizens enter with no eTA or visa at all, and requires everyone else to obtain a visitor visa (TRV, CAD 100) — visitors are normally allowed to stay up to 6 months.

passportValidity.text: The UK FCDO says your passport must be valid for the length of your planned stay in Canada.

source.name: UK FCDO — Canada travel advice (entry requirements)

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read makes travel insurance an entry requirement for visitors. The UK FCDO says medical treatment can be very expensive, that there are no special arrangements for British visitors, and advises insurance for local treatment or unexpected medical evacuation.

source.name: UK FCDO — Canada travel advice (health)

onwardTicket.text: The UK FCDO says Canadian border officials may ask you to show a return or onward ticket. IRCC says you must convince a border services officer that you will leave Canada at the end of your visit.

source.name: UK FCDO — Canada travel advice (entry requirements)

proofOfFunds.text: IRCC says you must have enough money for your stay; the amount varies with how long you stay and whether you stay in a hotel or with friends or relatives. You must also convince a border services officer that you have ties, such as a job, home, financial assets or family, that will take you home.

source.name: IRCC — Who can apply: basic requirements to enter Canada

currencyLimits.text: Currency and monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more (or equivalent) must be declared to CBSA on arrival and departure. There is no limit on the amount — only a reporting duty.

source.name: CBSA — Travellers: what to declare

notes: The Canada Border Services Agency says you must declare all food, plants, animal and related products. The UK FCDO says the Canadian authorities confiscate banned food products and you could be fined.
The UK FCDO says it is illegal to take cannabis across the Canadian border without a permit or exemption from Health Canada, even though recreational cannabis is legal in Canada.
The Canada Border Services Agency says you must declare all weapons and firearms at the port of entry, or the goods may be seized and you could face prosecution.

safety.text: The UK FCDO advises precautions against petty crime, such as not leaving bags unattended and keeping luggage out of sight in cars. It says terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Canada. Winter storms, including freezing rain and blizzards, make driving dangerous in many areas from November to April; wildfires are a risk especially in summer, and emergency help is limited in remote Arctic areas.

tips.text: IRCC says its official eTA application page is on canada.ca and that the eTA costs CAD 7. The UK FCDO says some unauthorised websites charge for submitting applications.
The eTA is only for air travel. If you drive or sail in from the US, visa-exempt visitors need only their passport. No eTA, no fee.

Never take cannabis across the Canadian border in either direction. The UK FCDO says it is illegal without a permit or exemption from Health Canada, and that people who try to take cannabis out of Canada without one face arrest.

faq.question: Do US citizens need an eTA or visa for Canada?
faq.answer: No. US citizens are exempt from both the eTA and the visitor visa. A valid US passport is enough, by air or land, for visits of up to 6 months.

faq.question: What is the Canadian eTA and how much does it cost?
faq.answer: The Electronic Travel Authorization is an online entry requirement for visa-exempt travelers flying to Canada. It costs CAD 7, is usually approved within minutes, and stays valid for up to 5 years or until your passport expires.

faq.question: Do Mexican citizens need a visa for Canada?
faq.answer: It depends. Mexicans qualify for the eTA (air travel only) if they have held a Canadian visa in the past 10 years or hold a valid US non-immigrant visa. Otherwise they must apply for a visitor visa (TRV, CAD 100).

faq.question: How long can I stay in Canada as a visitor?
faq.answer: IRCC says most visitors can stay up to 6 months, and the border services officer may limit or extend that. If your passport is not stamped, you can stay until 6 months from entry, the expiry of your passport or the expiry of your biometrics, whichever comes first. To stay longer, apply for a visitor record at least 30 days before your authorized stay ends.

faq.question: Do I need an eTA if I enter Canada by car from the US?
faq.answer: No. The eTA applies only to arrivals by air. Visa-exempt travelers crossing by land or sea just need a valid passport; travelers from visa-required countries need a visitor visa regardless of how they arrive.
